nativePlatform.colorSerialization: DESIGN.md colors are dynamic native API identifiers, intentionally not CSS values. Resolve them with AppKit/SwiftUI.
nativePlatform.previewPolicy: No HTML/CSS replicas or synthetic tonal ramps: they would freeze or misrepresent macOS-native rendering. Component entries document native implementation and are not browser-renderable previews.

narrative.overview:
ChatType’s control panel is a useful, candid personal studio: readable service facts, restrained navigation and native macOS controls. Its AppKit window hosts SwiftUI content. System typography, dynamic system colors and SF Symbols (Apple’s system icon library) support everyday operation while the existing product name and brand assets remain owner-controlled.

This document records the implemented settings surface of 0.5.1 (122), using `PreferencesWindowController.swift`, `TerminologyEditor.swift` and `ProcessingFlowView.swift`. It covers the reusable control-panel language, not the recording overlay or a new visual direction. Page strategy remains in `docs/control-panel-surface.md`; product commitments remain in `PRODUCT.md`.
keyCharacteristics: Dynamic macOS semantic surfaces and one system accent.
Compact system typography with a clear title, section and detail hierarchy.
Flat grouped content, small rounded rows and native control behavior.
Local feedback beside its action; configuration save state in the persistent bottom bar.

rules.name: Native Color Rule
rules.body: Keep system colors dynamic; resolve appearance through AppKit and SwiftUI rather than freezing sampled light-mode RGB values.

rules.name: Native Type Rule
rules.body: Use the macOS system font and the observed semantic or point-size roles; preserve the native title hierarchy.

rules.name: Flat Grouping Rule
rules.body: Use semantic background contrast and native dividers for structure; content cards and rows do not add custom shadows.

dos: Do preserve the product name, app icon, dynamic menu-bar icon and existing brand colors.
Do use native buttons, fields, pickers, toggles, focus treatment and disabled states.
Do accompany readiness and errors with meaningful labels or symbols.
Do show operation feedback near the action and configuration save status in the bottom bar.
Do reset the page scroll position when changing sidebar destinations.
donts: Don’t freeze dynamic semantic colors into sampled hex values.
Don’t substitute decorative display fonts for the native operating interface.
Don’t invent custom hover colors, shadows or motion for controls that use system defaults.
Don’t treat a local “Read names” result as proof that configuration was saved.
Don’t change owner-controlled brand visuals without explicit approval.
